# SVVV University Academic Regulations 2026

## 1. General Academic Framework

### 1.1 Purpose

The Academic Regulations of SVVV University establish the general rules governing undergraduate and postgraduate academic programs. These regulations describe requirements related to enrollment, attendance, examinations, academic progression, assessment, grading, and completion of academic programs.

Every enrolled student is expected to understand and follow the academic regulations applicable to their program. Students are responsible for checking official notices, academic calendars, departmental instructions, and examination announcements issued by the University.

### 1.2 Applicability

These regulations apply to all regular students enrolled in undergraduate, postgraduate, diploma, and cer

regulations apply to all regular students enrolled in undergraduate, postgraduate, diploma, and certificate programs unless a specific program regulation states otherwise.

Where a program has additional requirements, the department may issue supplementary academic instructions. Such instructions must be communicated to students through an official University channel.

### 1.3 Academic Year

The academic year normally consists of two regular semesters. The University may also conduct summer terms, special academic sessions, or supplementary examinations when required.

The dates of commencement, teaching periods, examinations, vacations, and registration activities are published in the academic calendar.

Students are expected to complete registration within the period specified by the Un

emic calendar.

Students are expected to complete registration within the period specified by the University. Failure to complete required registration may result in restrictions on participation in academic activities.

---

## 2. Student Enrollment and Registration

### 2.1 Enrollment

A student becomes an enrolled member of the University after completing the prescribed admission and registration requirements.

Enrollment may require submission of academic documents, identification information, photographs, fee payment, and other documents specified by the University.

The University may verify submitted documents at any stage. If information submitted during admission is found to be incorrect or fraudulent, appropriate disciplinary or administrative action may be taken.

### 2.2 Semest

rrect or fraudulent, appropriate disciplinary or administrative action may be taken.

### 2.2 Semester Registration

Students must register for their courses during the registration period announced by the University.

A student who does not complete semester registration within the prescribed period may be prevented from attending classes or appearing in assessments until the registration issue is resolved.

Late registration may be permitted by the University in exceptional circumstances. The University may prescribe a late registration fee.

### 2.3 Course Selection

Students must select courses according to the curriculum applicable to their program and semester.

Students must satisfy prerequisite requirements before registering for a course that has prerequisites.

The academic depar

rerequisite requirements before registering for a course that has prerequisites.

The academic department may advise students regarding suitable course combinations. However, students remain responsible for checking whether their selected courses satisfy program requirements.

### 2.4 Adding or Dropping Courses

A student may request to add or drop a course during the period specified in the academic calendar.

Requests submitted after the permitted period may require approval from the Head of Department or another authorized academic officer.

Dropping a course does not automatically remove financial obligations associated with the course.

---

## 3. Attendance and Academic Participation

### 3.1 Attendance Recording

Attendance is recorded by the faculty member or another authorized aca

### 3.1 Attendance Recording

Attendance is recorded by the faculty member or another authorized academic representative.

Students are expected to attend scheduled lectures, laboratory sessions, tutorials, practical classes, workshops, and other compulsory academic activities.

Attendance may be recorded using electronic systems, classroom registers, biometric systems, or other methods approved by the University.

### 3.2 Attendance Requirement

Students are expected to maintain the minimum attendance percentage prescribed by the University and their academic program.

For regular academic courses, attendance is calculated using the number of academic sessions attended compared with the total number of sessions conducted.

Students should regularly review their attendance records and repo

al number of sessions conducted.

Students should regularly review their attendance records and report apparent errors to the relevant faculty member or department within the period specified by the University.

### 3.3 Attendance Shortage

A student whose attendance falls below the required level may be declared ineligible for one or more academic assessments.

The department may notify students who have attendance shortages and may provide an opportunity to submit supporting documents where permitted by University rules.

Attendance shortage does not automatically disappear because a student performs well in internal assessments or examinations.

### 3.4 Academic Participation

Attendance alone does not constitute satisfactory academic participation.

Students may also be required to par

alone does not constitute satisfactory academic participation.

Students may also be required to participate in laboratory work, presentations, assignments, tutorials, projects, seminars, and other academic activities.

Failure to complete compulsory academic activities may affect eligibility for assessment.

---

## 4. Assessment and Evaluation

### 4.1 Continuous Assessment

Academic performance may be evaluated through multiple forms of assessment, including quizzes, assignments, laboratory work, presentations, projects, class tests, mid-semester examinations, and end-semester examinations.

The exact distribution of marks is determined by the curriculum and course structure.

### 4.2 Internal Assessment

Internal assessment is conducted during the teaching period.

Faculty members are

ernal Assessment

Internal assessment is conducted during the teaching period.

Faculty members are responsible for communicating assessment requirements to students. Students must submit assignments and complete assessments within the deadlines announced by the relevant course instructor.

Late submissions may receive reduced marks or may not be accepted when the course rules do not permit late submission.

### 4.3 End-Semester Examination

The end-semester examination is conducted according to the University examination schedule.

Students must satisfy eligibility requirements before appearing in the examination.

The examination schedule, examination center, reporting time, and permitted materials are communicated through official examination notices.

### 4.4 Practical and Laboratory A

materials are communicated through official examination notices.

### 4.4 Practical and Laboratory Assessment

Courses containing practical or laboratory components may require students to complete experiments, laboratory records, demonstrations, practical examinations, or project work.

A student may be required to complete the practical component separately from the theory examination.

---

## 5. Grading and Academic Progress

### 5.1 Grades

Students receive grades based on their performance in assessments conducted for each course.

The grading system may include letter grades, grade points, marks, or other evaluation methods approved by the University.

The grading scheme applicable to a course should be communicated through the official course information.

### 5.2 Passing a Course

a course should be communicated through the official course information.

### 5.2 Passing a Course

A student must satisfy the minimum passing requirements prescribed for the relevant course.

Some courses may require students to achieve separate minimum requirements in theory and practical components.

Passing one component does not necessarily compensate for failure in another component when separate passing requirements are prescribed.

### 5.3 Academic Progress

Students are expected to make satisfactory academic progress toward completion of their program.

Academic progress may be evaluated using semester performance, cumulative performance, failed courses, credit completion, and other criteria defined by the University.

Students who do not satisfy academic progression requirements

r criteria defined by the University.

Students who do not satisfy academic progression requirements may be required to repeat courses, attend additional academic sessions, or follow an academic improvement plan.

---

## 6. Examination Conduct

### 6.1 Examination Hall

Students must report to the examination venue within the reporting time stated in the official examination instructions.

Students must carry the identification or examination documents required by the University.

Students must follow instructions given by examination staff.

### 6.2 Permitted Materials

Only materials specifically permitted in the examination instructions may be brought into the examination hall.

Electronic devices may be restricted or prohibited during examinations.

Students are responsible for checki

ic devices may be restricted or prohibited during examinations.

Students are responsible for checking examination instructions before entering the examination venue.

### 6.3 Academic Integrity

Students must complete examinations, assignments, projects, and other academic work honestly.

Plagiarism, unauthorized collaboration, impersonation, fabrication of information, use of unauthorized materials, and other forms of academic misconduct may result in disciplinary action.

The University may investigate suspected academic misconduct according to applicable procedures.

---

## 7. Leave and Academic Absence

### 7.1 Academic Leave

Students who are unable to attend academic activities for a permitted reason may submit a leave request through the procedure prescribed by the University.

Ap

permitted reason may submit a leave request through the procedure prescribed by the University.

Approval of leave does not automatically guarantee exemption from attendance requirements or academic assessments.

### 7.2 Supporting Documents

Where supporting documentation is required, students must submit the documents within the prescribed period.

The University may verify submitted documents before approving an absence or leave request.

### 7.3 Extended Absence

A student expecting to remain absent for an extended period should inform the department as soon as reasonably possible.

The department may provide academic guidance regarding missed coursework, assessments, laboratory work, and examinations.

## 8. Academic Records

### 8.1 Student Records

The University maintains academic records for enrolled students.

Academic records may include course registrations, attendance records, assessment results, examination results, grades, credits, and academic progression information.

### 8.2 Correction of Records

A student who believes that an academic record contains an error may submit a correction request to the appropriate department or administrative office.

Requests should contain sufficient information to identify the suspected error.

The University may review relevant records before approving any correction.

### 8.3 Confidentiality

Academic records should be handled according to applicable University policies and legal requirements.

Access to academic inf

handled according to applicable University policies and legal requirements.

Access to academic information may be limited to authorized students, faculty members, administrators, examination officials, and other authorized persons.

---

## 9. Academic Appeals

### 9.1 Right to Appeal

A student may appeal an academic decision where an appeal process is specifically provided by University regulations.

The appeal must be submitted within the prescribed period.

### 9.2 Appeal Procedure

An appeal should clearly state the decision being challenged and the reason for requesting review.

Supporting documents may be attached where relevant.

The authorized academic committee or officer may review the appeal and issue a decision according to University procedures.

### 9.3 Final Decision

### 9.3 Final Decision

Where the applicable regulation identifies an appeal decision as final, no further internal appeal may be available.

Students should consult the relevant departmental or University office for the applicable appeal procedure.

---

## 10. General Provisions

### 10.1 Official Communication

Students must regularly monitor official University communication channels.

Important academic information may be communicated through the University website, student portal, institutional email, notice boards, or official departmental announcements.

### 10.2 Interpretation of Regulations

Where a provision requires interpretation, the matter may be referred to the appropriate academic authority.

Students

requires interpretation, the matter may be referred to the appropriate academic authority.

Students should not assume that informal advice overrides an official University regulation.

### 10.3 Amendments

The University may amend academic regulations when required.

Amendments should be communicated through appropriate official channels and may become effective from the date specified in the relevant notification.

### 10.4 Responsibility of Students

Every student is responsible for understanding the regulations applicable to their program.

Failure to read an applicable regulation does not normally constitute an exemption from compliance.

### 10.5 Effective Date

These Academic Regulations are designated as the general academic framework for SVVV University for the 2026 academic year.

# Attendance Policy

## 1. Purpose

The University Attendance Policy establishes minimum attendance requirements for students enrolled in undergraduate and postgraduate programs. Regular attendance is considered an essential part of academic learning because classroom participation, laboratory work, tutorials, discussions, and other academic activities contribute to the overall educational experience.

The policy applies to all students unless a specific academic program has an approved additional attendance requirement.

---

## 2. Minimum Attendance Requirement

### 2.1 Standard Attendance Requirement

Every student must maintain a minimum attendance of **75%** in each registered course during an academic semester.

Students whose attendance falls below 75% may be declared ineligible to

ring an academic semester.

Students whose attendance falls below 75% may be declared ineligible to appear for the end-semester examination in that course.

Attendance is calculated using the total number of scheduled academic sessions conducted by the department.

---

## 3. Attendance Recording

Faculty members are responsible for recording attendance for every scheduled lecture, tutorial, laboratory, practical session, or other compulsory academic activity.

Attendance should normally be recorded at the beginning or during the academic session.

Students are responsible for checking their attendance records regularly through the University's academic portal.

Any discrepancy in attendance records should be reported to the concerned faculty member within seven working days.

---

## 4. S

records should be reported to the concerned faculty member within seven working days.

---

## 4. Shortage of Attendance

Students who have attendance below the required percentage will receive an attendance shortage notification.

A student with attendance shortage may submit a written request to the Head of Department explaining the reason for the shortage.

The request must include supporting documents where applicable.

The Head of Department may review the request and forward eligible cases to the appropriate academic authority.

---

## 5. Medical and Exceptional Cases

### 5.1 Medical Absence

Students who are absent because of illness may submit valid medical documents to the department.

Medical documents should normally be submitted within seven working days after the student re

ment.

Medical documents should normally be submitted within seven working days after the student returns to academic activities.

The University may verify medical documents before considering an attendance concession.

### 5.2 Participation in University Activities

Students representing the University in officially approved sports, cultural, technical, academic, or other activities may apply for attendance consideration.

Such participation must be approved by the relevant University authority.

### 5.3 Medical Attendance Exemption

In cases involving serious medical conditions and prolonged medically certified absence, an approved medical exemption may allow a student to appear for an examination with attendance as low as **60%**.

The exemption is applicable only when the required med

amination with attendance as low as **60%**.

The exemption is applicable only when the required medical documents have been submitted and the case has been formally approved by the competent academic authority.

This provision is intended for exceptional medical circumstances and does not automatically apply to every medical absence.

---

## 6. Attendance Concession Procedure

A student seeking attendance concession must submit an application through the prescribed University procedure.

The application should mention:

- Student name and enrollment number
- Course and semester
- Dates of absence
- Reason for absence
- Supporting documents
- Details of the faculty or department concerned

The department will verify the application before forwarding it to the competent authority.

Approva

The department will verify the application before forwarding it to the competent authority.

Approval of an attendance concession is not automatic.

---

## 7. Eligibility for Examination

Before each end-semester examination, the department will prepare an attendance eligibility list.

Students satisfying the minimum attendance requirement will normally be permitted to appear for the examination.

Students below the required attendance percentage may be withheld from the examination unless an approved exemption or concession applies.

---

## 8. Attendance Disputes

Students who believe that their attendance has been incorrectly recorded may submit a written complaint to the concerned faculty member.

If the issue is not resolved, the student may approach the Head of Department.

The deci

ty member.

If the issue is not resolved, the student may approach the Head of Department.

The decision of the department may be reviewed by the designated academic committee according to University procedures.

---

## 9. Student Responsibilities

Students are expected to:

1. Attend all scheduled academic sessions.
2. Monitor their attendance regularly.
3. Inform faculty members about genuine absences.
4. Submit required documents within the specified period.
5. Avoid providing false or misleading attendance information.
6. Follow department-specific attendance procedures.

---

## 10. Important Rule

The standard University attendance requirement is **75%**. Exceptional medical cases may be considered under the approved medical exemption procedure described in Section 5.3.

All attenda

be considered under the approved medical exemption procedure described in Section 5.3.

All attendance concessions remain subject to verification and approval by the competent authority.

# Discipline Policy

## 1. Introduction

The University Discipline Policy establishes standards of conduct for students and defines procedures for dealing with violations of University rules.

Students are expected to behave responsibly and respectfully on campus, in classrooms, laboratories, hostels, University events, and other places where they represent the University.

---

## 2. Student Conduct

Students must:

- Respect faculty members, staff, visitors, and other students.
- Follow reasonable instructions issued by authorized University officials.
- Protect University property.
- Maintain academic and personal integrity.
- Follow safety and security requirements.
- Avoid behavior that disrupts academic activities.

---

## 3. Prohibited Conduct

The following activities may be treat

disrupts academic activities.

---

## 3. Prohibited Conduct

The following activities may be treated as violations of University discipline:

1. Physical violence or threats.
2. Harassment or intimidation.
3. Damage to University property.
4. Theft or unauthorized use of property.
5. Disruption of academic activities.
6. Unauthorized access to restricted areas.
7. Misuse of University information systems.
8. Submission of false information.
9. Violation of examination rules.
10. Repeated violation of hostel regulations.

---

## 4. Academic Misconduct

Academic misconduct includes behavior that compromises the fairness or integrity of academic evaluation.

Examples may include:

- Plagiarism
- Unauthorized collaboration
- Fabrication of academic information
- Using unauthorized materials

sm
- Unauthorized collaboration
- Fabrication of academic information
- Using unauthorized materials during examinations
- Impersonation
- Submitting another person's work as one's own

Academic misconduct may be handled under the University's examination and academic integrity procedures.

---

## 5. Reporting a Complaint

Any student, faculty member, staff member, or authorized University representative may report a suspected disciplinary violation.

A complaint should provide sufficient information for the University to understand the alleged incident.

Where appropriate, supporting documents or other relevant evidence may be submitted with the complaint.

---

## 6. Preliminary Review

After receiving a complaint, the designated authority may conduct a preliminary review.

The purpose

fter receiving a complaint, the designated authority may conduct a preliminary review.

The purpose of the review is to determine whether the complaint requires further investigation.

The University may request additional information from the person making the complaint or from other relevant individuals.

---

## 7. Investigation

If further investigation is required, the competent authority may collect relevant information and communicate with the individuals involved.

The student concerned should normally be informed of the allegation and given an opportunity to provide an explanation.

The investigation should be conducted according to applicable University procedures.

---

## 8. Student Response

A student facing a disciplinary allegation may submit a written explanation within the

ent Response

A student facing a disciplinary allegation may submit a written explanation within the period specified by the University.

The explanation should address the relevant facts and may include supporting information.

Failure to provide a response within the specified period may result in the matter being considered on the basis of available information, subject to applicable procedures.

---

## 9. Disciplinary Committee

Serious disciplinary matters may be referred to a designated disciplinary committee.

The committee may review:

- The complaint
- Relevant documents
- Statements from involved individuals
- The student's explanation
- Other information considered relevant

The committee may make recommendations to the competent University authority.

---

## 10. Possible Disciplinary Actions

Depending on the nature and seriousness of the violation, disciplinary action may include:

- Written warning
- Formal reprimand
- Requirement to provide an undertaking
- Loss of specific privileges
- Academic or administrative penalties where permitted
- Suspension
- Other action permitted under University regulations

The severity of the action should take into account the circumstances and seriousness of the violation.

---

## 11. Temporary Measures

In circumstances where immediate action is necessary to protect students, staff, property, or the normal functioning of the University, temporary administrative measures may be taken.

Temporary measures are not necessarily

University, temporary administrative measures may be taken.

Temporary measures are not necessarily a final finding of misconduct.

The matter should continue through the applicable review or disciplinary procedure.

---

## 12. Appeal

A student affected by a disciplinary decision may have the right to appeal where an appeal mechanism is provided.

An appeal should normally:

- Identify the decision being challenged.
- Explain the grounds for appeal.
- Include relevant supporting information.
- Be submitted within the prescribed period.

The designated appellate authority will review the appeal according to University procedures.

---

## 13. Confidentiality

Disciplinary matters should be handled with appropriate confidentiality.

Information concerning an investigation should be shared

handled with appropriate confidentiality.

Information concerning an investigation should be shared only with individuals who are authorized or have a legitimate need to receive it.

Confidentiality does not prevent the University from taking necessary action or fulfilling legal and administrative obligations.

---

## 14. False Complaints

Submitting a complaint with intentionally false information may itself be treated as a disciplinary matter.

However, a complaint should not be considered false merely because the allegation could not be established after investigation.

The University should consider the available evidence before taking action regarding a complaint.

---

## 15. Digital Conduct

Students must use University digital systems responsibly.

Unauthorized access, misuse of

Conduct

Students must use University digital systems responsibly.

Unauthorized access, misuse of accounts, disruption of University systems, or deliberate attempts to compromise information security may result in disciplinary action.

Students must protect their account credentials and must not knowingly share access to University systems with unauthorized individuals.

---

## 16. Off-Campus Conduct

Students may be subject to University disciplinary procedures for serious conduct outside campus when the conduct has a direct and significant connection with University activities, safety, or reputation, subject to applicable rules.

---

## 17. Student Responsibilities

Students are expected to:

1. Follow University regulations.
2. Cooperate with legitimate investigations.
3. Provide tr

ed to:

1. Follow University regulations.
2. Cooperate with legitimate investigations.
3. Provide truthful information.
4. Respect the rights of other students.
5. Protect University property.
6. Follow academic integrity requirements.
7. Use University facilities responsibly.

---

## 18. Final Provision

The University may issue additional disciplinary procedures, notices, or guidelines when necessary.

Students are responsible for following the rules applicable to their academic program, campus facilities, and University activities.

# Examination Rules

## 1. Purpose

The Examination Rules define the procedures and requirements applicable to internal assessments, practical examinations, end-semester examinations, and other academic evaluations conducted by the University.

All students are expected to follow examination instructions issued by the University, school, department, and examination office.

---

## 2. Types of Assessment

Students may be evaluated through different forms of assessment, including:

- Internal tests
- Assignments
- Quizzes
- Laboratory work
- Practical examinations
- Presentations
- Projects
- Mid-semester examinations
- End-semester examinations

The weightage of each assessment component is determined according to the approved curriculum of the respective program.

Students must complete examination registration within the announced registration period.

A student may be required to clear applicable academic or administrative requirements before the examination form is accepted.

Students should verify their registered subjects before the final submission of the examination form.

---

## 4. Examination Eligibility

A student must satisfy the academic eligibility requirements prescribed by the University before appearing in an examination.

Attendance eligibility will be verified by the concerned department before the end-semester examination.

Students who do not satisfy the required attendance or approved exemption conditions may be decl

## 5. Examination Schedule

The examination office will publish the examination timetable through the official University communication channels.

Students are responsible for checking the examination schedule and reporting any timetable-related issue within the announced period.

Changes to the examination schedule may be made by the University when necessary.

---

## 6. Examination Hall Rules

Students must reach the examination venue before the reporting time mentioned in the examination instructions.

Students must carry their valid University identity card and examination authorization or admit card where required.

Only materials specifically permitted by the examination instructions may be brought into the examination hall.

Examination misconduct includes:

## 9. Academic Integrity

Students are expected to complete examinations and assessments honestly.

## 10. Absence from Examination

A student who is unable to attend an examination because of a serious and unavoidable circumstance should inform the department or examination office as soon as reasonably possible.

Supporting documents may be required.

Approval of an alternative examination opportunity is subject to University rules and the decision of the competent authority.

## 11. Practical and Laboratory Examinations

Students must follow the specific safety, attendance, equipment, and submission requirements applicable to practical examinations.

## 12. Results and Grades

Examination results will be published through the University's designated academic communication system.

Students should verify their results after publication.

Grades are awarded according to the approved grading system of the relevant academic program.

A student who believes that an examination result contains an error may apply for review, revaluation, or verification where such procedures are available.

Applications must be submitted within the period announced by the Universi

## 14. Supplementary and Repeat Examinations

Students who are eligible for supplementary, improvement, or repeat examinations may register according to the schedule announced by the examination office.

Eligibility depends on the academic regulations applicable to the student's program.

---

# Hostel Handbook

## 1. Introduction

The University Hostel provides residential facilities to eligible students. Hostel residents are expected to maintain discipline, cleanliness, safety, and respectful behavior within the hostel premises.

The hostel administration may issue additional instructions when required for the safety and proper management of residents.

---

## 2. Hostel Admission

Students seeking hostel accommodation must complete the hostel application process within the announced period.

Hostel allotment is subject to availability of rooms and eligibility requirements.

Students must provide accurate information during the hostel admission process.

A hostel room may be allotted only after the required administrative formalities have been completed.

---

## 3. Room Allot

otted only after the required administrative formalities have been completed.

---

## 3. Room Allotment

Rooms are allotted by the hostel administration.

Students must occupy only the room assigned to them.

A student must not transfer or exchange a room with another resident without written permission from the hostel administration.

Students are responsible for maintaining the furniture and other facilities provided in their rooms.

---

## 4. Hostel Timings

### 4.1 General Entry Rules

Residents are expected to follow the entry and exit timings prescribed by the hostel administration.

Students leaving the hostel premises should follow the applicable gate-entry and exit procedure.

### 4.2 Weekday Gate Closing Time

On weekdays, the hostel main gate closes at **9:00 PM**.

Residents

4.2 Weekday Gate Closing Time

On weekdays, the hostel main gate closes at **9:00 PM**.

Residents returning after the gate closing time may be required to provide a valid reason and obtain permission from the hostel staff.

Students should plan their activities accordingly.

---

## 5. Late Entry

A resident who expects to return after the prescribed hostel timing should inform the hostel administration whenever possible.

Late entry may require approval from the designated hostel authority.

Repeated late entry without valid reasons may result in disciplinary action according to hostel regulations.

---

## 6. Weekend and Holiday Rules

Hostel timings may be different on weekends, public holidays, and University holidays.

The hostel administration may publish special timing instruction

holidays, and University holidays.

The hostel administration may publish special timing instructions for such days.

Residents must follow the timing communicated for the relevant day.

---

## 7. Visitors

Visitors are permitted only according to hostel visitor rules.

Visitors may be required to register at the hostel reception or security desk.

Visitors must comply with security instructions.

Residents are responsible for the conduct of their visitors while they are inside the hostel premises.

---

## 8. Special Entry Provision

### 8.1 Academic and University Activities

Students participating in officially approved academic, sports, cultural, technical, or University activities may receive special permission for late entry.

The student may be required to provide evidence of parti

receive special permission for late entry.

The student may be required to provide evidence of participation in the approved activity.

### 8.2 Weekday Resident Entry

For residents returning from approved University activities, the hostel administration may permit entry until **10:00 PM on weekdays**.

Such permission is subject to verification of the activity and approval by the designated hostel authority.

This provision applies only to approved activities and does not create a general extension of hostel timing.

### 8.3 Emergency Situations

In emergencies, hostel staff may permit entry outside normal timings after verifying the circumstances.

Students should immediately contact the hostel administration or security staff when an emergency affects their expected return time.

## 9. Hostel Discipline

Residents must maintain proper behavior within the hostel premises.

The following activities are prohibited:

- Damaging hostel property
- Fighting or threatening other residents
- Creating excessive disturbance
- Unauthorized room changes
- Misusing hostel facilities
- Entering restricted areas
- Violating reasonable safety instructions

Disciplinary action may be taken for violations.

---

# Scholarship Policy

## 1. Introduction

The University Scholarship Policy provides financial assistance to eligible students based on academic performance, financial circumstances, special achievements, or other approved criteria.

Scholarships are subject to eligibility requirements, availability of funds, and approval by the competent University authority.

---

## 2. Types of Scholarships

The University may offer different categories of scholarships, including:

- Merit scholarships
- Need-based scholarships
- Sports scholarships
- Academic achievement scholarships
- Special achievement scholarships
- Government-supported scholarships
- Scholarships sponsored by external organizations

Each scholarship category may have separate eligibility and documentation requirements.

Students applying for a scholarship must satisfy the eligibility conditions specified for the relevant scholarship.

Eligibility may depend on:

- Academic performance
- Family financial circumstances
- Attendance
- Participation in approved activities
- Sports or cultural achievements
- Previous scholarship status
- Other criteria specified in the scholarship notification

Meeting the minimum eligibility conditions does not guarantee that a scholarship will be awarded.

demic performance.
